clue.text: School is beginning to mend split

indicators.note: the beginning of the word mend is its opening letter, taken here

explanation.surface: A school is starting to heal a rift among its staff or pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: A schism is a split or division within a group, especially a church.

clue.text: Security, for example, involving iron anklet ultimately

indicators.note: the phrase for example wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: say means for example, as in 'a fruit, say, an apple'
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: the final letter of the word anklet is taken

explanation.surface: Security measures might include fitting an iron tag on an ankle.
explanation.definitionFit: Safety is freedom from danger, much like security.

clue.text: Deaf old fellow's first to appear in severe part of court case

indicators.note: these letters show up inside the phrase for the court session, as a witness appears in court

parts.note: hard means severe or harsh
a hearing is a session of a court case

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word fellow's is taken

explanation.surface: An elderly man, who cannot hear, is the first witness in the toughest stage of a trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deaf' looks like it describes the old fellow, but it is the definition; 'to appear in' puts the inserted letters inside the court phrase, as a witness appears in court.
explanation.definitionFit: Being hard of hearing is having impaired hearing, partly or wholly deaf.

clue.text: Name borne by quiet anonymous Irish river

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet

indicators.note: the letter for name is carried inside the following words

explanation.surface: A river in Ireland carries a name that is hushed and unknown.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shannon is the longest river in Ireland.

clue.text: Plan to perform in an instant? Not quite

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step
the word for an instant is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a tick is a moment, as in 'back in a tick'
to act is to perform

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a plan can be carried out in a flash.
explanation.walkthrough: TIC (a tick, 'Not quite') goes round ACT; the word 'in' does double duty as the containment signal in the surface reading, so it is left as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactic is a planned manoeuvre or scheme for achieving an aim.

clue.text: A couple of books — Biblical books — shown by religious leader

indicators.note: a pair of the letter for books is wanted

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for book
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A monastic head is shown with a few volumes of scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'couple of' doubles B; OT is the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbot is the head of a monastery, a religious leader.

clue.text: Extraordinary to pleb, winning game

indicators.note: something extraordinary is out of its usual order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: It is remarkable that a common person is triumphing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extraordinary' signals rearranging all of TO PLEB WINNING.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenpin bowling is the indoor sport of rolling a ball at ten pins.

clue.text: Shout after covering each kilometre, making harsh sound

indicators.note: the word for shout wraps round the other letters

parts.note: to cry is to shout
K is the abbreviation for kilometre

explanation.surface: Someone yells after each kilometre run, rasping hoarsely.
explanation.definitionFit: Something creaky makes a grating, squeaking noise, like an old door.

clue.text: Weapon getting attention in company

indicators.note: the word for attention is placed inside the word for company

parts.note: a firm is a business company
to give an ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: A weapon draws notice when produced among other people.
explanation.definitionFit: A firearm is a gun, a weapon that fires shots.

clue.text: Rich person, one upset by probing magazines

indicators.note: the inner pieces push into the word for magazines

parts.note: mags is short for magazines

indicators.note: upset means the word by is turned over, reading backwards in a down clue

explanation.surface: A single person is distressed by prying gossip magazines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset by' looks like distress; it reverses BY to YB.
explanation.definitionFit: Moneybags is an informal name for a wealthy person.

clue.text: Quantity of wine, say, knocked back in boozy spree

parts.note: a bin is a quantity of wine stored together in a cellar

indicators.note: knocked back means the abbreviation for say is turned round

parts.note: EG (for example) is what say means here

explanation.surface: Wine is gulped down during a drunken night out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' looks like drinking, but it reverses EG. A bin is a cellar rack or lot of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A binge is a bout of heavy drinking, a spree of excess.

clue.text: Where you may see golfers run out in great quantity

indicators.note: the cricket shorthand is placed inside the word for a great quantity

parts.note: tons means a great deal, so a ton is a great quantity
RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out

explanation.surface: Golfers are seen pouring out onto the course in large numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: TROON is a Scottish seaside town with a famous Open Championship golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal Troon in Ayrshire hosts golf's Open Championship, so golfers are seen playing there.

clue.text: Criticise fool with a mining tool

parts.note: a nit is a fool or idiot, British slang
a pick is the pointed tool used for digging and mining

explanation.surface: Someone insults an idiot who wields a miner's implement.
explanation.definitionFit: To nitpick is to find fault over trivial details, a petty kind of criticism.

clue.text: Love to search a maze of rooms?

parts.note: honey is a term of endearment, like love
to comb an area is to search it thoroughly

explanation.surface: A sweetheart is invited to hunt through a labyrinth of chambers.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: a building riddled with rooms and passages is called a honeycomb.
explanation.definitionFit: A honeycomb is a mass of cells, so figuratively a warren or network of rooms.

clue.text: Unacceptable opinion in item not shown on TV?

parts.note: out means not acceptable, as in 'that's out'
a take is a view or opinion, as in 'my take on it'

explanation.surface: A shocking view is in a programme segment that never aired.
explanation.definitionFit: An outtake is a scene filmed but cut from the broadcast version.

clue.text: Commercial I ignored in broadcast TV aired

indicators.note: the letter I is left out of the pool before the shuffle
broadcast suggests scattering, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An ad was dropped from a show that went out on television.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I from TV AIRED, then rearrange TVARED.
explanation.definitionFit: An advert is a commercial, an advertisement on air or in print.

clue.text: Legal action about soldiers in line

indicators.note: the word for legal action goes around the army letters

parts.note: a case is a lawsuit
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: A lawsuit involves troops standing in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: A crease is a line made by folding, or a marked line in cricket.

clue.text: Doctor and a copper taking on the French vampire

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
la is French for the, feminine

explanation.surface: A doctor and a policeman take on a French bloodsucker.
explanation.definitionFit: Count Dracula is Bram Stoker's famous vampire.

clue.text: Canadian policeman allowing second to go free

indicators.note: allowing the short word for second to leave signals a removal
letting go means the short word for second is dropped

parts.note: a Mountie is a member of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police
a mo is a short moment, a second

explanation.surface: A Mountie lets someone go free after just a second.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie is to undo bonds, setting something free.

clue.text: One drawing a tall building

definitions.meaning: one who pulls or hauls something along, a tug or truck
a lofty structure, such as a church spire or castle keep

explanation.surface: An artist at work sketching a skyscraper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawing' suggests sketching, but here it means pulling: one who tows.
explanation.definitionFit: A tow-er hauls things; a tower is a tall, narrow building.

clue.text: Be a chauvinist, dismissing leader

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for a chauvinist is removed

parts.note: a sexist is a male chauvinist

explanation.surface: Someone is accused of acting as a bigot by sacking the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: To be and to exist both mean to have reality or life.

clue.text: Floor coverings rolled back in area displaying grit

indicators.note: rugs rolled back suggests reading the word for them backwards

parts.note: mats are floor coverings

explanation.surface: Rugs are rolled up in a space where someone shows determination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolled back' fits rugs, but reverses MATS to STAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Grit is endurance and determination, as is stamina.

clue.text: Row about two appearances of good friend to Pooh

indicators.note: the word for row goes round the doubled letter

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

indicators.note: the abbreviation for good shows up twice

explanation.surface: A quarrel concerns two showings by one of Winnie-the-Pooh's pals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel; it means a tier of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Tigger is the bouncy tiger among Winnie-the-Pooh's friends in A. A. Milne's books.

clue.text: Black bird and dog

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
an eagle is a bird of prey

explanation.surface: A dark-coloured bird and a dog are seen together.
explanation.definitionFit: A beagle is a small hound breed.
